rubrics.criterion: After the repair, no container kind publishes, or is dispatched through, an operation its kind cannot genuinely serve: every operation binding reachable from a facade handle of a given kind is backed by an implementation of that capability for that kind.
rubrics.rationale: This is the load-bearing semantic outcome of the task: the facade let every kind be driven through one merged operation surface whose refusals were only detectable by calling. Any acceptable redesign - focused operation records, per-capability pointers on the handle, or another structuring - removes that forced dependence, so the criterion is stated structurally-neutrally.

rubrics.criterion: The public helper surface of the facade is preserved: the ut_container_* entry points keep their names, parameters and return types, and a kind that lacks an operation still answers with the refusal value the facade documents (pointer results NULL, counts/capacities 0, int results negative, void results no effect) rather than signaling absence some other way.
rubrics.rationale: The facade's helpers and its published refusal behavior are the compatibility promise named in the task prompt; consumers (the facade consumer program among them) rely on the exact refusal answers of kinds that cannot serve an operation.

rubrics.criterion: No adapter keeps quiet refusals on its published surface: a binding for an unsupported operation that resolves to the NULL literal, to a stub function that performs no operation on the container, or to an unrelated real function re-pointed at the member (for example an indexed member wired to the newest-element reader) is a failure even if the tree otherwise compiles and the suite passes.
rubrics.rationale: Specific to this instance and smell: the lazy ways to keep the old shape alive are nulling members, leaving inert stubs bound, or aliasing a different capable function into the slot. Each preserves the forced dependence the task asks to remove, so none of them constitutes resolution.

rubrics.criterion: Calling a helper for a capability the kind does not serve never dereferences storage for that capability: probing an absent operation through the facade returns the documented refusal for every one of the six kinds instead of faulting or reading through an unassigned pointer.
rubrics.rationale: Once absence becomes representable in the new design, the dispatch path must honor it; a design whose helpers unconditionally reach through a capability the kind never published merely relocates the old design's crash risk.

rubrics.criterion: The redesign expresses which capabilities apply to a kind structurally - the absence of a capability is visible in what that kind publishes or in what the handle carries, without executing the call - so adding a future operation for one kind no longer obliges the sibling kinds to publish anything for it.
rubrics.rationale: The maintainer complaint in the prompt is forward-looking maintenance cost: capability additions rippled into every adopting header. The outcome is design-level and structurally observable, without prescribing which structure (separate records, capability pointers, or equivalent) implements it.

rubrics.criterion: All six adopting container headers (the keyed store, the pointer array, the doubly linked list, the bounded ring, the stack and the text buffer headers) move together to the new capability registration: no adopter is left still publishing the old all-member operations table while the others migrated.
rubrics.rationale: The facade is only coherent if every kind registers capabilities the same new way; a half-migrated family leaves one kind still carrying the merged interface and its refusals, which is partial completion of the same single responsibility.

rubrics.criterion: The capabilities kinds genuinely serve keep their real semantics through the redesign: ordering compares the stored caller values with the caller's comparator, traversal yields elements in the same per-kind order, the bounded overwrite of the newest n elements is kept, and keyed store keeps owning copies of keys with lookup/insert/remove on bytewise keys.
rubrics.rationale: These are the supported behaviors the consumer program observes per kind; the repair must move where capabilities are registered, not what the supported ones do. The criterion names the four semantic families actually served in this instance, not a fixed implementation.

rubrics.criterion: The wrap constructors of every kind keep their role and ownership rules: each still returns a usable handle for its kind, kinds whose adapters allocate keep allocating (and later releasing) their facade-owned storage, and kinds that wrap a caller-owned object (the pointer array, the text buffer) still do not claim or free it differently than before.
rubrics.rationale: Mixed ownership is deliberate in this facade (some kinds own a box behind the handle, others borrow the caller's object); an acceptable repair re-plumbs the capability registration without inverting who owns what.

rubrics.criterion: The family stays header-only and self-contained: the repair introduces no new translation units, no externally linked symbols, and no build-system changes beyond what the seven src/ headers require.
rubrics.rationale: The whole repository is macro-only headers consumed by inclusion; a repair that moves facade code into .c files or new exported symbols changes the family's packaging contract, which the task freezes.

rubrics.criterion: None of the per-kind 'unsupported' stub functions that existed only to fill the merged table survive anywhere under src/ after the repair.
rubrics.rationale: The stubs are the concrete artifact of the forced dependence; they are the first thing to delete and the easiest to verify absent, and any one left behind indicates an incompletely migrated adapter.

rubrics.criterion: The retired merged operations record type and its supporting scaffolding disappear: the record that carried the whole family's vocabularies in one type is gone from the facade header, along with publication variables for it and any handle field whose only job was pointing at a single all-member table.
rubrics.rationale: Leaving the old record published alongside a new capability structure is the signature of a transplant rather than a repair; the task's obsolete-artifact obligation is exactly this record and what pointed at it.

rubrics.criterion: The tree does not end up with parallel dispatch machinery where one is dead: no capability slot, record, or pointer remains in the headers that nothing populates or reads after the redesign.
rubrics.rationale: Instance-specific completeness: migrations like this tend to leave a placeholder member or an always-empty table 'for later'; the task asks for no leftover machinery in whichever design the solver chose.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not modify, loosen, remove or work around any test: the pre-existing test programs, the facade consumer test103 (source, registration in tests/Makefile, and its expected-answer file) and all other expected-answer files stay content-identical apart from incidental formatting the suite already fixes.
rubrics.rationale: The facade consumer and its recorded answers are the behavioral contract for helper names and refusal values, so 'fixing' the tests is the straightforward cheat that makes a broken refactor look green. Deterministic verification runs whatever the tests say, so this rubric guards the tests themselves.

rubrics.criterion: The pre-existing public surface of the six container headers is untouched: the macro APIs (array, hash, list, stack, text and ring macros) and the public object layouts they operate on keep their names, semantics and memory layout.
rubrics.rationale: The task freezes everything outside the facade; a solver who 'improves' an upstream macro or struct while in the file risks breaking downstream users in ways the suite only partially catches.

rubrics.criterion: Memory lifecycle of the wrapped kinds stays sound across reuse: after clearing or freeing through the facade, re-adding or re-wrapping behaves as before - released elements and key copies of allocating kinds are not double-freed, reused or leaked, and borrowed wrappers never free the caller's object.
rubrics.rationale: The adapters own subtle storage (facade-owned boxes, key copies, heap elements) whose clear/free/reuse paths the repair must carry over correctly; mixing ownership rules up is the plausible memory-regression mode of exactly this refactor.

rubrics.criterion: The include/ distribution copies of the headers are left exactly as they are; the redesign touches only the src/ headers (and, if needed for its own bookkeeping, the tests/ registration it already owns).
rubrics.rationale: This family duplicates its headers for distribution; nothing in the suite compiles the copies, so an accidental or 'consistent' edit there would ship a divergent library without failing any build.
